newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares slip on gvt reshuffle news.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares slip on gvt reshuffle news.

text.p: Dealers marked down prices of some Russian shares in the hope of speculative gains later after news President Boris Yeltsin had ordered a complete government reshuffle on Tuesday, but traders said the fall was short-lived.
At 1130 GMT Rostelekom slipped off its early highs of $4.10 to $4.02, LUKoil fell to $14.40 from $14.43 and Norilsk Nickel was $6.56 after $6.75.

Yeltsin ordered a full reorganisation of the government, leaving only Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais in place. The bulk of the government will be formed within one week, he said in a decree.
Traders said the news was a good opportunity for short-term speculation for Russian brokers.

"Shares went down while people are having lunch. When New York opens we shall go up again," said IFCI-Moscow Partners chief trader Alexei Abdurakhimov. "Chernomyrdin and Chubais are staying and the rest of the people in the government are not very important for the market."
Traders said Western investors were not worried by the coming reshuffle, taking no action on the market.

"Prices are changing in different directions. I have an impression that price changes are not connected to the presidential decree. I canot see any hasty actions on the part of investors," said Regent European Securities trader Alexander Fonarkov.
